title: 1994 AHSME Problem 27
statement: A bag of popping corn contains \(\frac{2}{3}\) white kernels and \(\frac{1}{3}\) yellow kernels. Only \(\frac{1}{2}\) of the white kernels will pop, whereas \(\frac{2}{3}\) of the yellow ones will pop. A kernel is selected at random from the bag, and pops when placed in the popper. What is the probability that the kernel selected was white?

solutions.text: The probabilities of selecting a kernel that pops are \[ \begin{gathered} P(W\text{ and pop})=\frac23\cdot\frac12=\frac13, \\ P(Y\text{ and pop})=\frac13\cdot\frac23=\frac29. \end{gathered} \] Hence \(P(\text{pop})=\frac{5}{9},\) and \[ P(W\mid\text{pop})=\frac{\frac{1}{3}}{\frac{5}{9}}=\frac35. \] Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: Compute the probabilities of selecting-and-popping for each color
Condition the white-and-popped probability on the total probability of popping
